root_cause.text: In __sctp_rcv_asconf_lookup(), the code does not verify that the variable-length address parameter declared in a truncated ASCONF chunk actually lies within the chunk bounds before calling from_addr_param(), which reads the full address (up to 16 bytes for IPv6) from uninitialized memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a bounds check: `if (sizeof(*asconf) + ntohs(param->p.length) > ntohs(ch->length)) return NULL;` and the commit explains that only the ADDIP header and a parameter header were checked, but not the full parameter body, allowing an unauthenticated peer to cause an uninit-value read.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a length check to prevent reading beyond the ASCONF chunk boundary when parsing the address parameter.
intent_record.what: Added a check to ensure that the address parameter in an ASCONF chunk fits within the chunk length before accessing it.
intent_record.how: Before calling af->from_addr_param(), the function now validates that sizeof(*asconf) + ntohs(param->p.length) does not exceed ntohs(ch->length); if it does, it returns NULL, preventing an out-of-bounds read from a truncated chunk.

candidates.rationale: This line creates a pointer to the address parameter without verifying that the chunk contains enough data, leading to an out-of-bounds pointer.
This line dereferences param->p.type, which can read out-of-bounds if the chunk is truncated, causing access to uninitialized memory.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement creates a pointer to the address parameter without verifying that the ASCONF chunk contains enough data to hold the full address parameter, leading to an out-of-bounds pointer when the chunk is truncated.
This statement dereferences param->p.type, which reads from uninitialized memory if the chunk is truncated, because param points beyond the chunk bounds.
